results.canonical_news_title: From 14 cities to 15,000: What it will take to scale robotaxis?

adjacent_competitors.name: Uber AV ecosystem
adjacent_competitors.reason: Robotaxi platform/ecosystem, not a local service-station turnaround readiness ledger.

competition_search_terms: robotaxi fleet service turnaround cleaning charging maintenance software
autonomous vehicle depot operations readiness checklist
results.market_gap: Fresh search found fleet/AV platforms and depot technology, but no direct standalone product for outsourced/local robotaxi turnaround checklist, defect escalation, readiness evidence and SLA proof.
results.mvp: Turnaround work orders, station checklist, defect/escalation queue, readiness evidence and SLA dashboard.
results.working_logic: Create vehicle arrival job; execute configurable clean/charge/reset/inspection checklist; log defects; require evidence/signoff; release vehicle and measure station SLA.
results.marketing_strategy: Target AV fleet service partners, depot operators and detailing/maintenance networks.
results.first_customer_plan: Pilot manually with one fleet-service/depot operator; configure one vehicle turnaround SOP.
results.main_risk: Market timing: addressable robotaxi operations remain geographically concentrated.
results.validation_assumption: Local partners need auditable release-to-service evidence rather than generic fleet maintenance.

competition_search_terms: robotics training dataset provenance management software demonstration session
physical AI robot data collection QA dataset card
results.market_gap: No direct same-workflow product found, but the triggering Korean development could not be re-verified strongly enough from an original/primary source in this validation pass.
results.mvp: Session registry, task/hardware metadata, provenance checklist, QA state and dataset-card export.
results.working_logic: Register each collection session; bind task/robot/sensors/operators; attach provenance/consent; run QA checklist; approve dataset slice; export dataset card.
results.first_customer_plan: Interview 5 robotics labs collecting teleoperation/demonstration data.
results.main_risk: Evidence strength of the trigger is insufficient for hard qualification.
results.validation_assumption: The product stores metadata/evidence, not large training binaries.
results.rejection_reason: Triggering development was only partially re-verified; hard evidence gate not met.

results.canonical_news_source: South China Morning Post / space-sector corroboration

adjacent_competitors.name: Orbit Fab
adjacent_competitors.reason: In-space refuelling infrastructure/provider; not a vendor-neutral mission readiness/evidence workflow product.

adjacent_competitors.name: Astroscale
adjacent_competitors.reason: In-orbit servicing provider; not standalone compatibility-gate/evidence software.

competition_search_terms: satellite in orbit refueling mission planning compatibility software
on orbit servicing readiness evidence management
results.market_gap: Providers exist for refuelling/servicing, but fresh search found no direct standalone vendor-neutral readiness/evidence desk matching candidate workflow.
results.mvp: Servicing candidate register, compatibility checklist, mission readiness gates, evidence vault and post-service record.
results.working_logic: Register spacecraft; capture interface/fuel/orbit constraints; run compatibility checklist; route technical/risk approvals; freeze evidence package; record servicing outcome.
results.marketing_strategy: Direct outreach to small satellite operators, servicing startups and space consultancies.
results.first_customer_plan: Pilot with one small satellite operator or servicing startup using a non-flight-critical readiness/evidence workflow.
results.main_risk: Very small customer universe and domain-expertise barrier.
results.validation_assumption: MVP is workflow/evidence management, not orbital dynamics or safety-critical mission control.

results.canonical_news_title: AI agents are exposing a security gap between the data they read and the systems they can change

global_competitors.name: Zenity
global_competitors.reason: Direct AI-agent security/governance: inventory, permissions, risk controls, monitoring and policy enforcement.

global_competitors.name: Lasso Security
global_competitors.reason: AI agent/application security governance with visibility, policy and controls over agent/tool behavior.

competition_search_terms: Türkiye AI agent security governance permissions approval audit
AI agent permissions governance tool inventory approval audit
results.market_gap: The exact agent inventory/permission/policy/audit job is already an active AI security product category.
results.mvp: Agent inventory, tool/permission matrix, risk-tier approvals, circuit-breaker register and audit export.
results.working_logic: Register agent and tools; map scopes/actions/data; classify risk; require approval; record safeguards and evidence; periodically review.
results.main_risk: Direct vendors have deeper runtime visibility/enforcement.
results.validation_assumption: A documentation-first SME version could be cheaper but does not create a clean market gap.
results.rejection_reason: Zenity and Lasso substantially overlap the same AI-agent permission/governance workflow.
